title: Charge of GST
outcomes: Explain the levy under the CGST and IGST Acts.
Identify supplies taxed under reverse charge and the ECO's liability.
Apply the eligibility, rates and conditions of composition levy.

meta.exam_tip: For reverse charge questions, check both the supplier's and the recipient's description — the entry applies only if both match.

concepts.title: Levy under section 9(1)–(2) and section 5 of the IGST Act
body: Section 9(1) of the CGST Act levies central tax on all intra-State supplies of goods or services, except alcoholic liquor for human consumption, on the value under section 15, at notified rates (up to 20% CGST), collected and paid by the taxable person. Section 5(1) of the IGST Act does the same for inter-State supplies (up to 40%), with IGST on imported goods collected under the Customs Tariff Act.
Section 9(2): GST on crude, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel applies only from a notified date.
Ordinarily the supplier pays (forward charge). Rates are notified by HSN/SAC on the Council's recommendation.
concepts.analogy: The charging section names the event (supply), the base (value), the rate and the person who pays.
concepts.work: Petrol remains outside GST until notified, though it is within the Constitutional definition.

concepts.title: Reverse charge (s. 9(3) and 9(4))
body: Section 9(3): for notified goods and services, the recipient pays tax instead of the supplier. Key services: goods transport agency services to specified recipients (factories, societies, registered persons, body corporates, firms, casual taxable persons) unless the GTA opts for forward charge; legal services by an advocate or firm of advocates to a business entity; arbitral tribunal services; sponsorship to a body corporate or firm; most services by Government to business entities; services by a director to the company; insurance agent to insurer; recovery agent to a bank or NBFC; author or music composer transferring copyright (unless the author opts to pay); security services by a non-body corporate to registered persons; business facilitator to banks; and renting of residential dwelling to a registered person.
Renting of other immovable property by an unregistered person to a registered person (other than a composition taxpayer) is also under reverse charge.

Section 9(4): for notified classes of registered persons, supplies received from unregistered suppliers of notified goods or services are under reverse charge — mainly promoters of real estate projects who fall short of the required purchases from registered persons.
The recipient must pay reverse charge tax in cash, issue a self-invoice where the supplier is unregistered and a payment voucher, and may take ITC if eligible.
concepts.analogy: Reverse charge moves the tax duty to the business side of the deal where the supplier is hard to police.
concepts.work: A small advocate need not register just because he advises companies — the companies pay the GST.

concepts.title: Tax payable by electronic commerce operators (s. 9(5))
body: Section 9(5): for notified services supplied through an e-commerce operator, the operator is liable as if it were the supplier. Notified services include passenger transport by radio taxi, motor cab, maxi cab, motor cycle and similar; accommodation in hotels, inns, guest houses and similar places (unless the supplier is registered); housekeeping such as plumbing and carpentry (unless the supplier is registered); and restaurant services.
An ECO without physical presence in the taxable territory acts through a representative or appoints one.
This differs from TCS under section 52, where the operator collects a small amount on supplies made by others through it.
concepts.analogy: For these services the platform steps into the supplier's shoes for GST.
concepts.work: A food delivery app pays GST on restaurant food ordered through it; the restaurant does not pay again on those orders.

concepts.title: Composition levy (s. 10)
body: Section 10(1): a registered person whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year did not exceed ₹1.5 crore (₹75 lakh in specified north-eastern and hill States) may pay a fixed percentage of turnover: manufacturers 1%, traders 1% of turnover of taxable supplies, restaurants (not serving alcohol) 5% — each split equally between CGST and SGST. Other services up to 10% of turnover or ₹5 lakh, whichever is higher, are allowed.
Section 10(2A): a person who supplies services (or mixed goods and services) not eligible under section 10(1) may opt for a 6% composition if preceding-year turnover did not exceed ₹50 lakh.

Not eligible: suppliers of non-taxable goods or services, inter-State outward suppliers, casual and non-resident taxable persons, suppliers of services through ECOs, and manufacturers of notified goods (ice cream, pan masala, tobacco products, aerated waters, fly-ash bricks, building stones and similar).

Conditions: no ITC; no tax collected from customers; "composition taxable person" displayed at the business place and on bills of supply; all registrations under the same PAN must opt together. Exceeding the limit during the year ends the option from that day.
concepts.analogy: Composition trades input tax credit and full invoicing for low, simple tax.
concepts.work: A sweet shop with ₹1.2 crore turnover that also caters at weddings (services up to 10%) can stay in composition.

illustrations.title: Three small businesses
illustrations.q: Compute composition tax for the year (all in Gujarat, preceding-year turnover within limits): (a) a trader with turnover of taxable supplies of ₹90 lakh; (b) a restaurant (not serving alcohol) with turnover ₹60 lakh; (c) an interior designer who opted under section 10(2A), with turnover ₹45 lakh.

solution.text: No ITC is available, tax cannot be collected from customers, and a bill of supply is issued instead of a tax invoice.

jobs.title: Reverse charge check-list
jobs.situation: A company's expense ledger has legal, transport, director and rent payments.
steps: Match each payment to the notified reverse charge list.
Pay RCM tax in cash by the due date.
Claim ITC in the same return if eligible.
jobs.takeaway: RCM tax is paid in cash, but often comes back as credit.

mcqs.explain: Section 9(1) excludes only alcoholic liquor for human consumption; the others are taxable at notified rates. In practice: alcohol bears State excise and VAT.
mcqs.topic: Levy under section 9(1)–(2) and section 5 of the IGST Act

mcqs.q: Legal services by an individual advocate to a business entity are taxed under:
options: Reverse charge — the business entity pays
mcqs.explain: Notified under section 9(3): the business entity recipient pays. Services to individuals not in business are exempt. In practice: check the recipient's turnover for exemptions.

mcqs.q: Services by a director to the company are taxed:
options: Not at all, being Schedule III
mcqs.explain: Non-employee director services are under reverse charge; services as an employee (whole-time director on salary) are in Schedule III. In practice: sitting fees attract RCM.

mcqs.q: A registered company rents an office from an unregistered landlord. GST is payable by:
mcqs.explain: Renting of non-residential property by an unregistered person to a registered person (other than a composition taxpayer) is under reverse charge. In practice: the company issues a self-invoice.

mcqs.q: Under section 9(5), GST on hotel accommodation booked through an app is paid by the app when the hotel is:
mcqs.explain: For accommodation and housekeeping services, the ECO is liable unless the actual supplier is registered. In practice: registered hotels pay their own tax.
mcqs.topic: Tax payable by electronic commerce operators (s. 9(5))

mcqs.q: Composition turnover limit for a trader in Kerala (preceding year):
mcqs.explain: Kerala is not among the specified States with a ₹75 lakh limit, so ₹1.5 crore applies. The ₹50 lakh limit is for section 10(2A) service providers. In practice: limits are on aggregate turnover across India under the PAN.

mcqs.q: Composition rate for a restaurant not serving alcohol:
mcqs.explain: Restaurants pay 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST) under composition; manufacturers and traders pay 1%; section 10(2A) service providers 6%. In practice: no ITC is available.

mcqs.q: Which person is NOT eligible for composition?
options: A trader making inter-State outward supplies
mcqs.explain: Inter-State outward supply disqualifies a person from composition. In practice: inter-State purchases are allowed.

mcqs.q: A section 10(2A) service provider can opt in if preceding-year turnover did not exceed:
mcqs.explain: Section 10(2A) is for service providers and mixed suppliers with preceding-year turnover up to ₹50 lakh, paying 6%. In practice: it also needs no inter-State outward supply.

summary: s. 9(1)/IGST s. 5: levy on supply, except alcohol for human consumption.
s. 9(3)/(4): reverse charge on notified supplies; pay in cash.
s. 9(5): ECO pays for cab, accommodation, housekeeping and restaurant services.
Composition: ₹1.5 crore (₹75 lakh special States); 1%/1%/5%; s. 10(2A) ₹50 lakh at 6%.
remember: Composition: no ITC, no tax collection, bill of supply.
Services up to 10% of turnover or ₹5 lakh allowed under s. 10(1).
traps: Rent from unregistered landlord not RCM for composition dealers.

viva.model: A mechanism under which the recipient, not the supplier, is liable to pay tax on notified supplies or on supplies from unregistered persons where notified.

viva.q: Can reverse charge tax be paid using ITC?
viva.model: No, it must be paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger, though the recipient may then take ITC of it if eligible.

viva.q: Name two services covered by section 9(5).
viva.model: Passenger transport by cab or motorcycle and restaurant services supplied through an e-commerce operator; accommodation and housekeeping too where the supplier is unregistered.

viva.q: What is the composition limit for a manufacturer?
viva.model: Aggregate turnover up to ₹1.5 crore in the preceding financial year, or ₹75 lakh in the specified States, with tax at 1% of turnover.

viva.q: What restrictions apply to a composition taxpayer?
viva.model: He cannot take input tax credit, cannot collect tax from customers, must issue bills of supply and must show that he is a composition taxable person.

cases.title: Hilltop Bakers
cases.case: Hilltop Bakers of Dehradun, Uttarakhand, had preceding-year turnover of ₹1.1 crore from intra-State sales of bakery products, plus ₹6 lakh from a small catering service. It hires a goods transport agency for deliveries and rents its shop from an unregistered owner. It wants to opt for composition.

options: Yes, turnover is within ₹1.5 crore and services are within 10%
mcqs.explain: Uttarakhand has the ₹1.5 crore limit; catering of ₹6 lakh is below 10% of turnover or ₹5 lakh, whichever is higher (10% of ₹1.16 crore = ₹11.6 lakh). In practice: watch turnover during the year.

mcqs.q: As a composition dealer, can Hilltop take ITC on ovens?
mcqs.explain: Composition taxpayers cannot take any ITC. In practice: consider this before opting if capital purchases are large.

mcqs.q: Rent paid to the unregistered owner, once Hilltop is under composition:
options: Not taxed under reverse charge in Hilltop's hands
mcqs.explain: Reverse charge on renting of non-residential property by an unregistered person excludes recipients under composition. In practice: check the landlord's status every year.

options: Bills of supply marked as composition taxable person
Tax invoices showing CGST and SGST
mcqs.explain: A composition taxpayer issues bills of supply without charging tax and declares his status. In practice: also display it at the shop.
